Read Wildlife Acoustics metadata

Source: R/wamd.R
wamd.Rd

Reads the wamd chunk of a wave file, the metadata Wildlife Acoustics Song Meter recorders write: the model of the device, its serial number, the firmware it was running, the prefix of the filename it wrote, the time the recording started with the offset from UTC the device was set to, the position its receiver had, the microphone fitted and the identifications their software has since made. A file holding no wamd chunk gives an empty result rather than an error.

Usage

wamd(x)

Arguments

x

Path to a wave file, a Wave object with wamd metadata attached, a raw vector holding a wave file, or a wamd object

Value

A wamd object, which is a named list of fields

Details

The chunk names its fields by number rather than by name. The names used here are those of the reference implementation published with the GUANO specification; a field this package has no name for is reported under its number, as wamd:21.

The embedded voice note, the program the device was running and the state it was left in are binary rather than text and are passed over. Their sizes are kept on the result as its "binary" attribute, so that a file carrying them can be told from one that does not.

See also

readMetadata() reads this and every other metadata format a file carries at once. guano() reads the GUANO metadata that current Wildlife Acoustics firmware writes in place of this format, and parseFilename() reads the filename conventions of these recorders.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
m <- wamd("S4U09011_20210712_043000.wav")
m[["timestamp"]]
} # }
